scheme_name: RKVY Soil Health and Fertility - Soil Health Card
description:
The RKVY Soil Health and Fertility initiative is a significant component of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) launched by the Government of India in 2007.

The primary objective of this scheme is to promote sustainable agriculture through the enhancement of soil health and fertility.

The Soil Health Card (SHC) scheme was launched on February 19, 2015.

The initiative aims to provide farmers with detailed information about the nutrient status of their soil.

It also aims to guide them on the appropriate dosage of fertilizers to be used for various crops.

The Soil Health Card is issued to farmers every two years.

The card contains information on the nutrient status of the soil.

It provides recommendations for the application of fertilizers and soil amendments.

The Soil Health Card scheme is designed to improve the productivity of crops.

It aims to ensure that farmers can make informed decisions regarding soil management.

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

The Soil Health Card is provided free of cost to farmers.

The initiative targets all farmers across India.

The scheme is particularly beneficial for small and marginal farmers.

Farmers can receive a Soil Health Card by applying through their local agricultural department.

The application process involves submitting a request to the local agriculture officer.

Farmers must provide details about their land and previous crop history.

Soil samples are collected from the farmer's field for testing.

The samples are analyzed in designated soil testing laboratories.

The results are compiled and presented in the Soil Health Card.

Farmers are advised on the necessary corrective measures based on the soil test results.

The Soil Health Card includes specific recommendations for NPK (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium) fertilizers.

It also provides information on secondary and micronutrients.

The scheme aims to reduce the overuse of chemical fertilizers.

It encourages the use of organic fertilizers and practices.

The Soil Health Card is part of a broader strategy to promote sustainable agricultural practices.

The government aims to cover all farmers under the Soil Health Card scheme by 2025.

As of 2021, over 22 million Soil Health Cards have been distributed across India.

The scheme has a budget allocation of INR 500 crore for the financial year 2021-2022.

The Soil Health Card is expected to enhance the income of farmers by improving crop yields.

Farmers are encouraged to adopt soil health management practices.

The initiative also aims to promote the use of bio-fertilizers.

The Soil Health Card scheme is linked to the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana.

This linkage aims to ensure efficient water use in conjunction with soil health management.

The government has set a target of issuing 12 million Soil Health Cards annually.

The Soil Health Card is valid for two years.

Farmers are advised to retest their soil every two years to keep the information updated.

The Soil Health Card scheme is crucial for achieving the goal of doubling farmers' income by 2022.

The scheme is also aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

The Soil Health Card is an essential tool for promoting precision farming.

Farmers can access their Soil Health Card information online through the official portal.

The government encourages the use of mobile applications for easy access to soil health information.

The Soil Health Card scheme has received positive feedback from farmers.

Many farmers report increased awareness about soil health due to the scheme.

The initiative has also led to a reduction in the use of chemical fertilizers.

The Soil Health Card scheme is supported by various state governments.

State governments are responsible for implementing the scheme at the grassroots level.

The scheme has been instrumental in promoting organic farming practices.

Farmers are educated about the importance of soil health through various outreach programs.

The Soil Health Card scheme is part of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture.

The government conducts training programs for farmers on soil health management.

The Soil Health Card includes a detailed analysis of soil pH, electrical conductivity, and organic carbon content.

Farmers are encouraged to adopt crop rotation and intercropping based on soil health recommendations.

The scheme aims to improve the overall health of the agricultural ecosystem.

The Soil Health Card is a step towards achieving food security in India.

The initiative is expected to enhance the resilience of farmers against climate change.

The government collaborates with agricultural universities for research and development related to soil health.

The Soil Health Card scheme has been recognized internationally for its innovative approach.

Farmers can also access information on pest management and crop diseases through the Soil Health Card.

The initiative promotes the use of local indigenous practices for soil management.

The Soil Health Card is a vital resource for farmers in making informed agricultural decisions.

The scheme is continuously monitored and evaluated for its effectiveness.

The government aims to expand the Soil Health Card scheme to include more parameters in the future.

The Soil Health Card is a comprehensive tool for sustainable agricultural development in India.

The initiative reflects the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of farmers.

The Soil Health Card scheme is a significant step towards achieving agricultural sustainability in India.
